Load 9: little-endian update target $9279. The resident indirect jump at $0450, the last step of a main-loop pass, takes it while the game-exit flag $0840 is zero, the selected player's meter $4DCD,X is nonzero and the status $5284 that $7B84 returns is nonzero. Load 9: player frame byte $66. $6C4A stores it at $4A and stores the value minus $66 modulo 256 at $1177.

Load 9: the player's starting X low, X high and Y bytes, $31, $01 and $B2. $6C31–$6C3E copies them to $47–$49. At stage start $03B8–$03C4 also tests the X bytes: when X high is zero and X low is below $AB, $03C6 sets $4D6A to 7, otherwise to 0.

Load 9: the map's row stride in bytes, $43. The scroll routines add it to the map source pointer at $2D35 and $2D62 (scrolling right) and $2E2A and $2E57 (left), and $4738 uses it as the offset of the lower pair when $471B writes a stage record's two-by-two block of metatiles.

Load 9: the map's width in metatiles, $43. The rightward-scroll check at $0EF7–$0F02 compares the metatile column just past the view's right edge with it and skips the scroll when that column is not smaller, and the entity rightward move at $4593 undoes a move whose next column equals it.
The downward-scroll check at $0CCC–$0CD9 compares the next map-row position with this value.

Load 9: the view origin, column $5F and row $0C in characters. The screen builder $6D17 halves them at $6D26 and $6D2B to find the first metatile to draw; $6D8B–$6DA0 copies them to the left and top view bounds and computes right and bottom by adding $25 and $12 modulo 256; $6DA3–$6DBE scrolls once more down or right for an odd row or column; and $6DC1–$6DD6 stores the final bounds, adding $26 and $13. $33EC–$3408 saves both bytes, puts the current view's left and top ($569B, $569D) there for $6D17 to redraw the screen, and restores them.
The little-endian address $BD54 of this load’s entity records. $1863 copies it into the pointer at $E2–$E3.

The initial entity-slot limit is 4. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 4 ($18CB). The load has 4 entity records, all of which the initializer loads, stopping at the zero byte after them; each pass, the slot scan at $3622 checks slots 1 to 4 ($3629), and since no record follows, $3632 finds that zero byte and reloads an empty slot's own record at $366A.

A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and ($5A) at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

Load 9: the first 16 low bytes of the split map-row pointer table at $85CF; the matching high bytes begin at $8620. These entries point to $8671 through $8A5E in 67-byte steps. The drawing path reads the pair at $6D30–$6D39. The remaining entries are described separately.

Load 9: low bytes for pointer entries 16–79 of the 81-entry split table. Paired with the high table, these encode $8AA1 through $9B1E in 67-byte steps modulo 65536, the row stride at $7F4A. They lie beyond the map’s 16 rows, the count at $7F4C. The window draw at $6D30 and the scroll readers at $2CD4, $2DC9, $2EC2 and $2F9D index by the view’s rows, which the scroll check at $0CCC keeps within the map. The hero’s tile checks index the table by his row $6F3D ($0EA7, $1041, $6E77) or that row plus one ($0C47, $0C69, $6E8D); $6F3D reaches 16 when the view is at the bottom of the map and the hero at his lowest screen position $E1 ($0CFC), so entries 16 and 17 can be read, and no hero check reaches entries 18–79. The entity collision checks at $451D and $4638 index the table by an entity’s tile row from $71DB, plus one to three, with no bound of their own.

Load 9's stage-object record 3 names $95C4 in its bytes 7 and 8 ($93BB), which $4655 copies to $477D/$4783, and the shield purchase at $9F82 calls the routine those fields name.

Two jump entries: $978F enters the price setup at $9795, and $9792 jumps to the item-pair setup at $98B5. Write $46 plus 1 modulo 256 to the high address byte at $9AF4 of the digit store at $9AF2 and to the layout gate at $9B3E, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and use stage index $7B to format fields $4783,X and $4789,X through $97F8 with Y=$9B and Y=$AF as the screen offsets of their last digits.
Use selected-player index $4DBD. If $4DC7,Y is nonzero, or if $4DC9,Y is at least stage field $4789,X under an unsigned byte comparison, go to $97E3. Otherwise inspect stage field $4753,X.
Reached when stage field $4753,X is 3 or has bit 0 clear: select message $9C2D and jump to the message call at $9A7F.

Reached when stage field $4753,X is not 3: test its bit 0. A clear bit selects message $9C2D; a set bit calls $9AC6, which stores $FF in $4753,X, then selects message $9C17 and jumps to the message call at $9A7F.

Reached from the balance check when the gold covers stage field $4789,X. Test bit 0 of stage field $4753,X: clear selects message $9BD9, set selects $9BC2. Both jump to $9972, which shows the message and starts the choice loop.

Save X in the immediate operand at $9820 and Y in the one at $981B, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $9B39, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. A tens code of 1 is written as zero. Restore Y, call $9AE0, restore X and return.

The flags come from the selection byte $9B3F, loaded at $9A0B before the only jump here ($9A0E, taken when the layout gate $9B3E is nonzero): negative ($FF, left) enters the first-price balance check at $9854; zero selects message $9C00 at $98A2; otherwise (1, right) take the second-price path at $9826.

Reached from $9822 when the shop selection byte is 1. Load X from $7B and call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, record byte 9, the second price: $78D1 subtracts it in packed decimal from the selected player’s gold and restores the gold if that borrows. Reload X and read callback high byte $4771,X. If nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $9844 from $476B/$4771 (record bytes 4 and 5), clear the high byte in the stage record so that the callback runs only once, and call the patched target; then use A=4 at $9897, which adds it to the life meter. If zero, enter the message path at $984B, which shows message $9C6E and then does the same with A=4. In load 9, stage record 2 at $93A4 names this shop’s entry $978F, with second price $05 and callback $93E4.

Second-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9C6E (“Nice and cold, / is'nt it?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=4 and jump to $9892, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 4 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $9833 branches here when the callback high byte $4771,X (record byte 5) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the second price, record byte 9, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. In load 9 stage-object record 2 at $93A4 names the price set-up $978F as its callback.

If selected-player high balance $4DC7,Y is zero and low balance $4DC9,Y is less than stage field $4783,X under an unsigned byte comparison, jump to $9992. Otherwise continue to the first-price payment at $9869.

Reached from the balance check at $9854, which the selection path sends here when the shop selection byte is $FF and lets through when the selected player’s gold covers the first price. Call $78D1 with stage field $4783,X, record byte 8, the first price, which $78D1 subtracts in packed decimal from the gold, and reload the stage index. If callback high byte $477D,X is nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $9885 from $4777/$477D (record bytes 6 and 7), clear that high byte so that the callback runs only once, and call the target; then use A=8 at $9897, which adds it to the life meter. Otherwise enter the message path at $988C, which shows message $9C89 and then does the same with A=8. In load 9, stage record 2 at $93A4 names this shop’s entry $978F, with first price $15 and callback $9430.

First-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9C89 (“How do you like / the cocktail?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=8 and fall into $9892, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 8 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $9874 branches here when the callback high byte $477D,X (record byte 7) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the first price, record byte 8, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. In load 9 stage-object record 2 at $93A4 names the price set-up $978F as its callback.

Push A, call $77E0 with the message pointer in X/Y and pull A, then continue at $9897, which adds A to the player’s meter through $77A9. The second-price fallback jumps here from $9851 with A=4 and message $9C6E; the first-price fallback falls in from $988C with A=8 and message $9C89.

Call $77A9 with A=4 or A=8, reload stage index, decrement $4753,X and jump to $9A82. The two price paths jump here, $9848 with A=4 and $9889 with A=8, after paying. $77A9 adds A to the selected player’s life meter $4DCD,Y, capped at the limit $4DCF,Y; $9A82 calls $3C2A and $370B until the message countdown $4D6B is zero and returns. In load 9 stage record $93A4 names this shop’s entry.
Load X/Y with message pointer $9C00 and jump to the message call at $9A7F. $9824 branches here when the selection byte read at $9A0B is zero.

Reload stage index, decrement $4753,X, load message pointer $9C4A in X/Y and jump to the message call at $9A7F. The only jump here is from the timeout path at $99B7, taken when the layout gate $9B3E is nonzero.
Store zero at the layout gate $9B3E, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and set $4D69 to 7. Reload stage index from $7B and continue to the item-pair selection at $98C6. The jump entry at $9792 leads here.

Read $476B,X. If nonzero, pass it and $4771,X separately through the conditional-item resolver at $9A8E; store the returned values at $9B44/$9B45, then jump to $9903. If zero, branch to the implicit pair at $98DF.

Use $4771,X, byte 5 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, as Y. Clear carry, add the selected player $4DBD (0 or 1) and then $D5, and store the sum as the low byte of the LDA at $98F3; store $4D plus the carry as its high byte. Load 9's records on this path, record 3 at $93B4 and record 5 at $93D4, have 2 and 4 in byte 5, so neither addition carries and the LDA reads the selected player's byte of $4DD7 or $4DD9.

Read the absolute address patched by $98E9 and $98F0, $4DD5 plus stage field $4771,X plus the selected player index; clear carry and add $9B46,Y, where Y is that stage field. Store the result at $9B44, then store that result plus one modulo 256 at $9B45. Continue at $9903.

Load the second item's number from $9B45, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and read the picture-routine address at offsets 2 and 3 of its row in the 24-row item table at $9E95. Patch the JSR operand at $9919/$991A. Load 9's shop records give second items 7–12 and 14–18 here, all rows of the table: record 3 at $93B4 gives the selected player's $4DD7 byte (0–4) plus 13 and that plus one; record 5 at $93D4 gives the selected player's $4DD9 byte (0–5) plus 6 and that plus one.

Multiply A, the second item's number that $9903 loads from $9B45, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9E97,Y and $9E98,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $9918, which calls it with A=$E4. Load 9's shop records give items 7–12 and 14–18 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9E95.
Call the patched target with A=$E4. Then read the first item byte at $9B44, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and patch the JSR operand at $9931/$9932 from the same pointer table.

Multiply A, the first item's number that $991B loads from $9B44, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9E97,Y and $9E98,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $9930, which calls it with A=$D0. Load 9's shop records give items 6–11 and 13–17 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9E95.
Call the second patched target with A=$D0, then set the temporary row counter at $9E94 to 3 and begin filling colour RAM.

For each of three rows, write colour 9 to four bytes at $D8F8,Y and four at $D90C,Y. Y starts at zero and advances by 40 after each row; the counter at $9E94 ends at zero. With I/O visible, these are colour RAM writes. The next setup continues at $9952.
Store $46 plus one modulo 256 at $9AF4. Pass the first selected item at $9B44 to $9AFB, then call $9AE0 with Y=$73. Repeat for the second item at $9B45 with Y=$87.

Call $77E0 with the message pointer selected by the preceding path, then fall through to the mode and countdown initializer at $9975. The item-pair path loads $9B4B; the price path jumps here from $97EE or $97F5 with $9BD9 or $9BC2.

Store 0 in the selection byte at $9B3F, store $DC in the countdown at $9B43, and fall through to the wait path at $997F. Besides this store, only the left and right handlers write the selection byte, and they keep it among $FF, 0 and 1.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $9B43 and branch to $99B2 when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9AB6 and $9AA3; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $9992. Starting from the initialized $DC, the countdown reaches zero on the 220th call to $3C2A, counting the calls of this loop and of the one at $9992 together.
Call $3C2A, decrement $9B43 and branch to $99B2 at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9AB6 and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $99A3.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $9A06; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $99C8; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $99E6. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $9992. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.

Reached when the countdown at $9B43 reaches zero. If $9B3E is nonzero, jump to $98A9. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $9B80, and jump to the $77E0 call at $9A7F.

If the signed mode byte at $9B3F is negative, return to the wait path at $997F. Otherwise decrement it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9B3E is zero, pass the item index at $9B44 to the message selector at $9ACE. Call $9AB6 and return to the wait path.

If the mode byte at $9B3F equals 1, return to the wait path at $997F. Otherwise increment it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9B3E is zero, pass the item index at $9B45 to the message selector at $9ACE. Call $9AB6 and return to the wait path.

Read the layout gate $9B3E; if nonzero, load the selection byte $9B3F and jump to $9822. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $9B3F. If nonzero, branch to the purchase index choice at $9A2F, preserving the negative flag from that read. If zero, inspect $4753,X: a negative value or a clear bit 1 selects message pointer $9BA8; a nonnegative value with bit 1 set selects $9B91. Both paths jump to the $77E0 message call. $9B3E is $46 plus one on the price path ($979B) and zero on the item-pair path ($98B7).
Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $9B44 when it is set, or $9B45 when clear, then enter the price selector at $9A3A. The path at $9A06 supplies that flag from $9B3F.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the item row's price at $9E95,Y and $9E96,Y (row offsets 0 and 1) to $7D/$7E. Call $7901, which subtracts the packed-decimal amount from the selected player’s gold, restores it on insufficient funds, returns carry set on success and clears decimal mode. The code at $9A2F passes the first item's number from $9B44 when the selection byte is negative, or the second item's from $9B45. Load 9's shop records give items 6–18 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9E95.

After the $7901 price subtraction, jump to $997F on clear carry. On set carry, load X from $7B and decrement $4753,X with eight-bit wrap. Read $9B3F; if negative select the item index at $9B44, otherwise select $9B45. Push it and continue to the offset-4 routine-pointer selector at $9A64.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's purchase-routine address at $9E99,Y and $9E9A,Y (row offsets 4 and 5) into the operand of the JSR at $9A78, which calls it with the item number plus 1 in A. A is the bought item's number, pushed by the code before: the first item from $9B44 when the selection byte is negative, otherwise the second from $9B45. Load 9's shop records give items 6–18 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $9E95.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector. Load X/Y with $9B6D and call $77E0, then call $3C2A and $370B repeatedly while $4D6B is nonzero. Return once it is zero.
Load 9: return A unchanged unless it equals $13. For $13, inspect bit $10 of the selected player’s flags: return $14 when set, or $13 when clear. The shop item-pair path uses this resolver.

Load 9: call the input sampler at $3C4C and return carry set if any of $73, $74 or $70 is zero, carry clear if all are nonzero. The sampler reads joystick port 2 active-low, so carry is set while the stick is pushed left or right or fire is pressed.

Load 9: with decimal mode clear, add one to the selection byte at $9B3F, use the wrapped result as an index into $9B40, and pass that position in X and $82 in Y to $719E. The selection byte stays among $FF, 0 and 1, so the index is 0 to 2.

Multiply A, an item's number, by 8 using three eight-bit shifts, clear carry, add 6 and use the eight-bit result as X. Read the high byte from $9E96,X into Y and the low byte from $9E95,X into X, the message pointer at offsets 6 and 7 of the item's row in the 24-row item table at $9E95, then jump to $77E0. The selection paths call this routine at $99DD with the first item's number from $9B44 and at $99FD with the second's from $9B45. Load 9's shop records give items 6–18 here, all rows of the table: record 3 at $93B4 gives the selected player's $4DD7 byte (0–4) plus 13 and that plus one; record 5 at $93D4 gives the selected player's $4DD9 byte (0–5) plus 6 and that plus one.

Load 9: process four price-display bytes at $9B39 in reverse order. Leave zero unchanged; add $F5 to each nonzero byte with eight-bit wrap and decimal mode clear. Call the digit writer at $9AF2 with successive Y positions, decrementing Y after each call.

Load 9: store A at offset Y of the page after $46, through STA $FF00,Y. $9798 and $9955 each set its high byte $9AF4 to $46 plus one, $C1 or $C5, since $46 holds the screen page $C0 or $C4; the load holds $FF there. Then write colour 1 to $D900,Y, the matching colour RAM, and return. Called from $9AEA. Colour RAM requires I/O visible.

Load 9: multiply item ID A by eight with eight-bit wrap, split the two packed bytes from the item table at $9E95 into four nibble-plus-one values at $9B39, and replace consecutive leading ones with zero. Nibbles and item indexes are not locally validated.

Load 9: four working price-display bytes. The item-price formatter at $9AFB and the stage-price formatter at $97F8 write them, and the drawing loop at $9AE0 reads them in reverse, from $9B3C down to $9B39, passing each to the digit writer at $9AF2.

Load 9: mutable shop layout gate. Timeout, selection and purchase code read this byte to choose alternate paths.
Load 9: mutable shop selection byte. The input loop initializes it to zero, left and right paths update it, and the cursor helper indexes the position table using this value plus one.

Load 9: three cursor-position bytes, $5F, $B4 and $FF, for selections $FF, 0 and 1: the cursor helper at $9AB6 reads them at $9ABF with the selection byte plus one as index, and passes the byte in X to $719E. No instruction writes them.
Load 9: mutable shop timeout. The input loop initializes it to $DC and decrements it during both input-release and polling paths.

Load 9: mutable first item ID. $98D0 or $98FA stores it; the item drawing at $991B, the price label at $9958, the left-selection description at $99DA and the purchase paths at $9A37 and $9A60 read it.

Load 9: mutable second item ID. $98D9 or $9900 stores it; the item drawing at $9903, the price label at $9963, the right-selection description at $99FA and the purchase paths at $9A31 and $9A5A read it.

Load 9: five item-index offsets, $00, $00, $0D, $00 and $06, at $9B46–$9B4A. ADC $9B46,Y at $98F7 adds the selected offset to the player-state value and stores the first item ID; the following addition of one supplies the second ID, with Y equal to stage field $4771,X. Load 9’s two records on this implicit path, record 3 at $93B4 and record 5 at $93D4, have 2 and 4 there, so the load reads only $9B48 and $9B4A.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Welcome!” / “May I help you?” / “”, then the control byte $20. Load 9, shop message 6: three zero-terminated fields "" / "  Cocktail or Beer." / "", followed by control byte $10. Load 9, shop message 8: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10. Load 9, shop message 10: three zero-terminated fields "Come back" / "with some money." / "", followed by control byte $10.
